title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: late declaration fee amount and the single charge per declaration
content:
## Rule
Under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product the late declaration fee is the category's late declaration fee in full, and a late submission is charged at most once: when a late-declaration-fee row already references the judged declaration, nothing further is charged. The fee is a whole tariff amount stated to two decimal places and is not rounded further. The fee is owed only where the judged declaration is late and the acceptance is under review and no row yet references that declaration; in every other case the amount is 0.00.

## Late declaration fee by category
| Category | Late declaration fee (USD per acceptance) |
|---|---|
| AHL DG Limited Quantity | 150.00 |
| AHL DG Class 9 Standard | 250.00 |
| AHL DG Flammables and Corrosives | 350.00 |
| AHL DG Toxics and Oxidizers | 450.00 |
| AHL DG Compressed Gases | 450.00 |
| AHL DG Special Approval | 900.00 |

## Truth table
| A late-fee row already references the judged declaration | Declaration late | Acceptance under review | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | any | any | 0.00 |
| no | yes | yes | the category's fee in full |
| no | yes | no | 0.00 |
| no | no | any | 0.00 |

## Worked case (hypothetical, AHL DG Compressed Gases)
An acceptance under review has a late judged declaration and no late-fee row: the amount is 450.00. After that row is booked referencing the judged declaration, the amount found for the same declaration is 0.00.

## Points of judgement
- *A late-fee row exists but references a different declaration — does it stop the charge?* No; only a row that references the judged declaration means the late submission has already been charged.
